analysis: Examined three files. (1) DaemonStateFile.swift: DaemonState gains optional diagnostic fields enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery (initializer lines ~370-413). The file is written with the pre-existing `data.write(options: .atomic)` to the state path. No new write path, permissions or secrets were added. The new fields carry model IDs, timestamps and blocker strings. These are the same class of data as the existing advertisedModels and servingSelection, and the same pre-existing exposure (A-018, TB-003 local operator reads). The base file was not supplied in full, so I could not verify whether the earlier file permissions changed. This PR did not change them. (2) SelectedModelRecovery.swift (new): a pure in-memory scheduler struct with a backoff table (30s to 600s), a 120s victim-idle minimum and a pause recheck. It also adds the Codable SelectedModelRecoveryEntry. There is no I/O, crypto, network or privilege code. Backoff bounds the retry rate (T-029 and T-016 availability). The `attempt` Task is cancelled at shutdown according to its comment. The caller, ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery, was not supplied. Eviction of idle unselected models, the load-gate interaction and consumer-triggerable churn live in that unseen file, so they remain an integration question. The affected threats would be T-029 and the model-load availability concerns. (3) StartupPreloader.swift: Summary gains failedInsufficientMemory and notAttempted. The `isInsufficientMemoryLoad` helper changes from private to internal. The `run` loop now records the remaining candidates when `canLoadMore` returns false. There is no change to the admission logic, which still never evicts, or to the self-test fail-open/closed behavior. No trust-boundary, attestation, encryption, key, prefix-cache (T-041) or authorization behavior changed. No regressions identified. Remaining question: unseen ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery eviction policy and its handling of the add-on hold (TB-012, T-059) and the load fence.
